transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 08:15 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Wu (Montgomery Bank), Asha Kumar (Montgomery Bank), Ben Torres (Montgomery Bank)
Recording note: Call recorded via Fireflies; auto-transcription -- medium quality, some misheard acronyms

Summary (auto): Weekly security/check-in for POC. Focus on SSO test, audit logging export, retention config for pilot, and SOC2 evidence. Action items and timelines discussed.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Lena): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, and then we'll go through the SSO tests and logs.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Hi Lena, hi Ravi, yep here. Asha and Ben are on as well.
00:33 Speaker 1 (Lena): Great. quick agenda: SAML / SSO progress, audit log exports, retention defaults for pilot, then SOC2 and KMS questions.
00:48 Speaker 3 (Ravi): I'll start with the SSO, we ran the initial SAML handshake last night with the test IdP, there were a couple attribute mapping mismatches. The NameID was coming over as an email, but your IdP is sending uid, so we have to adjust the mapping or accept both.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Asha): Yep that matches what we saw, the SAML metadata you provided had the attribute name spelled as uid and the Redwood metadata expects email. small mapping change on our side should do it.
01:26 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We're going to push a config variant to the staging POC cluster - note that in the Redwood console (sometimes the transcription says Red wood console or Red wood inferance) the config page shows attribute mapping. you can toggle allow-alias on the mapping.
01:48 Speaker 5 (Ben): When can we run an IdP test window where we can do an end-to-end login? We're blocked on enabling user role mappings for a few pilot users.
02:03 Speaker 1 (Lena): How about next Monday? 2025-08-11 is free for the team per the calendar invite. we'll aim for a 30-minute IdP test slot.
02:20 Speaker 4 (Asha): Works for us, we'll confirm but tentatively ok.
02:35 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Moving to audit logs: we pushed a sample export to the shared drive earlier, but I want to walk through the schema. the main fields we capture: timestamp (ISO), request_id, route, model_variant, user_id (redacted for pilot), token_count, latency_ms, decision_reason (if fallback happened), and an event_type for auth, inference, config_change.
03:00 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Asha had asked specifically about including the full prompt or partial prompt in logs. Are you redacting prompt text by default?
03:14 Speaker 3 (Ravi): For the pilot we default to no full-text capture: we capture prompt hashes and truncated context (first 256 chars) unless customer opts in to full-text for troubleshooting. That behavior can be configured per env.
03:32 Speaker 4 (Asha): We need the audit log to include a consistent user identifier so our SIEM can correlate events, but we cannot accept PII in the logs. Can you provide pseudonymized user_id and mapping?
03:50 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yes, we can emit a pseudonymized UUID for user_id and provide a separate mapping file that stays on your side or is only accessible via secure KMS-wrapped transfer. for the pilot we'll do pseudonymized IDs.
04:05 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Good. also what retention window are you using in the sandbox pilot? we don't want logs stored indefinitely.
04:18 Speaker 3 (Ravi): By default pilot logs are retained 30 days in the shared S3, and can be shortened to 7 days. for Dedicated or production you can set your retention with lifecycle rules. we'll include retention options in the doc we send.
04:40 Speaker 4 (Asha): SOC2 evidence: we need to see the most recent type 2 report and the scope — specifically whether the hosted control plane or only the data plane is in scope.
04:58 Speaker 1 (Lena): We'll attach the SOC 2 letter and the scoping doc to the shared drive; current scope covers the hosted control plane and our platform services, but the private deployment package has a different scoping note. I'll confirm the exact control boundaries.
05:18 Speaker 5 (Ben): For the POC, Montgomery Bank wants to test both hosted and dedicated variants. does SOC2 cover the dedicated pools?
05:30 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Dedicated pools are in scope if they are managed by Redwood in hosted account. if you self-host the private package, then you'll have your own compliance responsibilities — we provide guidance. we'll be explicit in the doc.
05:46 Speaker 4 (Asha): KMS question — all logs and model artifacts, is that encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys or Redwood keys during the pilot?
05:59 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Pilot environments default to Redwood-managed keys but we can bring-customer-managed keys (BYOK) for dedicated pilots. for the private on-prem bundle you can use your HSM. we'll include KMS options and the extra cost in the pricing addendum.
06:19 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Does Redwood provide field-level encryption for prompts if we need it?
06:29 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Not field-level by default; we recommend application-side encryption for sensitive prompt data. we can advise on tokenization and partial redaction. we do support envelope encryption with customer keys for storage.
06:47 Speaker 4 (Asha): RBAC mapping — we need role mapping that maps your roles to our directory groups. can you provide a sample RBAC matrix?
06:58 Speaker 3 (Ravi): yes, we'll send a sample RBAC mapping matrix. it will include role names, permissions, admin vs viewer flags, and mapping to SAML group attributes.
07:15 Speaker 5 (Ben): Any concerns about latency when we enable stronger encryption or KMS calls?
07:27 Speaker 3 (Ravi): KMS calls can add a small CPU latency on some paths but they are async for storage operations; inference path encryption (like envelope decryption on host) is optimized. Dedicated pools with local KMS gateways reduce latency. we'll provide benchmark numbers in the doc.
07:48 Speaker 1 (Lena): On the commercial side, Asha you flagged an add-on for encryption. we'll send a pricing addendum for Dedicated pilot including BYOK and enhanced retention.
08:00 Speaker 4 (Asha): Also want to confirm who at Redwood will be the point for InfoSec evidence requests during the POC.
08:10 Speaker 1 (Lena): That's me for commercial and coordination; Ravi will handle technical evidence and the log samples. For audit requests we'll coordinate with our compliance team.
08:23 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Can you walk through the audit log sample now? we uploaded the file but a quick verification would help.
08:30 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Sure, opening the sample: the first entry is an auth event with event_type: auth.success, timestamp, user_pseudo_id, route: /v1/chat, model_variant: redwood-medium-v1, token_count: 42, latency_ms: 180. you might see slightly different model names in the transcript because of auto transcription like Redwood-medium vs Redwood Medium.
09:00 Speaker 4 (Asha): Looks OK. will you include the decision_reason field when we have fallback to smaller models? we need to see why a fallback happened for troubleshooting.
09:12 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Yes decision_reason is included. we also capture cpu/gpu_id for infra traces in the debug logs (not in the default prod audit stream) but for the POC we can include them in the sample.
09:30 Speaker 5 (Ben): About data residency, the sandbox was provisioned in us-west-2; we need EU residency for production. is there any limitation with the current setup?
09:45 Speaker 3 (Ravi): No — region pinning is supported. the current pilot in us-west-2 is fine, and we can replicate or move production workloads to eu-central-1 for residency requirements. we'll call out any multi-region replication caveats.
10:00 Speaker 4 (Asha): A few nitty-gritty items: 1) can logs be exported over SFTP to our SIEM? 2) can we have hashed prompt payloads instead of truncated text? 3) what's your incident notification SLA?
10:16 Speaker 3 (Ravi): 1) yes SFTP or direct S3 push is supported. 2) hashed payloads yes we support SHA-256 prompt hashing. 3) incident SLA: POC level is our standard incident channel; we'll share the real SLA options for Dedicated/Enterprise in the doc.
10:40 Speaker 1 (Lena): Ok let's capture the agreed dates: we'll send SOC2 and scoping doc by end of day Fri 2025-08-07; SE to upload trimmed audit log sample by 2025-08-08; IdP test window scheduled 2025-08-11. any blockers to that?
10:58 Speaker 4 (Asha): nothing on our side, just confirm time for the IdP test slot.
11:06 Speaker 2 (Daniel): we'll coordinate internal calendar invites after this call.
11:12 Speaker 1 (Lena): Great. Anything else?
11:20 Speaker 5 (Ben): Quick thing — are there any known gaps for SOC2 if we run a dedicated pilot? we want to prepare questions for procurement.
11:30 Speaker 3 (Ravi): We'll compile a short memo on SOC2 scoping for Dedicated vs Private; include procurement checklist items (network diagrams, data flows, SAML metadata).
11:44 Speaker 1 (Lena): Perfect. Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and the action items.

End of transcript.
